description.value: This voxel-based morphometry study investigated whether gray matter volume alterations in acutely traumatized patients predict later posttraumatic stress disorder symptoms, using whole-brain and region-of-interest analyses.

spans.text: Another focus was to identify structural patterns that could be predictive for the later development of PTSD symptoms.

value: A significant negative correlation was found between the GMV of a cluster located in the left lateral, middle, and superior temporal gyrus at T1 and hyperarousal symptoms at T2.

Considering the significant negative association between GMV in the lateral temporal regions at T1 and hyperarousal symptoms at T2, it is possible that disturbed cognitive processing about others as well as disturbed environmental object and motion detection leads to uncertainty in daily life, which accordingly results in hyperarousal.

spans.text: In the first preprocessing step, T1-weighted images from all participants were segmented into gray matter, white matter, and cerebrospinal fluid based on the tissue probability map implemented in the toolbox [ 66 ]. A data quality check was then performed to ensure that the segmentation and normalization procedures produced utilizable data. The covariance was used to check sample homogeneity. Finally, the gray matter images were smoothed (8-mm full width at half maximum).
